facts.statement: The genus Irritator was described by Martill et al. in 1996.
facts.quote: authority: Martill et al., 1996

facts.statement: The genus name Irritator refers to the irritation paleontologists felt because the skull was heavily damaged and altered by fossil collectors.
facts.quote: The genus name comes from the word "irritation", reflecting the feelings of paleontologists who found the skull had been heavily damaged and altered by the collectors

facts.statement: The species name challengeri honors the fictional character Professor Challenger from Arthur Conan Doyle's novels.
facts.quote: The species name is a homage to the fictional character Professor Challenger from Arthur Conan Doyle's novels

facts.statement: Irritator was identified as a spinosaurid theropod in 1996.
facts.quote: In 1996, the animal was identified as a spinosaurid theropod

facts.statement: Irritator belongs to the Spinosaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Both Irritator and Angaturama belong to the Spinosaurinae subfamily

facts.statement: Irritator was estimated to be between 6 and 8 meters long and weigh around 1 ton, making it one of the smallest known spinosaurids.
facts.quote: Estimated at between 6 and 8 m in length, Irritator weighed around 1 t, making it one of the smallest spinosaurids known

facts.statement: Irritator had a long, shallow, and slender snout lined with straight, unserrated conical teeth.
facts.quote: Its long, shallow and slender snout was lined with straight and unserrated conical teeth

facts.statement: A thin sagittal crest ran along the top of Irritator's head, likely serving as an anchor for powerful neck muscles.
facts.quote: Lengthwise atop the head ran a thin sagittal crest, to which powerful neck muscles were likely anchored

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Irritator likely preyed mainly on fish and other small animals it could catch.
facts.quote: Irritator might have preyed mainly on fish and any other small prey animals it could catch

facts.statement: Fossil evidence indicates an individual Irritator ate a pterosaur, either by hunting or scavenging.
facts.quote: Fossil evidence is known of an individual that ate a pterosaur, either from hunting or scavenging it

facts.statement: Irritator likely had semiaquatic habits and inhabited a tropical coastal lagoon environment surrounded by dry regions.
facts.quote: Irritator may have had semiaquatic habits, and inhabited the tropical environment of a coastal lagoon surrounded by dry regions

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Irritator was found near Santana do Cariri in northeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: The holotype of Irritator was excavated from a chalk concretion containing the rear of a large skull with lower jaws near the town of Santana do Cariri in northeastern Brazil.

facts.statement: The fossil was acquired by traffickers and taken to the State Museum of Natural History in Stuttgart, Germany.
facts.quote: This fossil was acquired by fossil traffickers and taken to the State Museum of Natural History in Stuttgart, Germany.

facts.statement: Irritator challengeri was first scientifically described in February 1996 by David M. Martill, Arthur R.I. Cruickshank, Eberhard Frey, Philip G. Small, and Maria Clarke.
facts.quote: The skull (designated SMNS 58022) became the holotype specimen of the new genus and species Irritator challengeri in February 1996, when it was first scientifically described by paleontologists David M. Martill, Arthur R.I. Cruickshank, Eberhard Frey, Philip G. Small and Maria Clarke.

facts.statement: The species name challengeri honors Professor Challenger, a character from Arthur Conan Doyle's novel The Lost World.
facts.quote: The type species, Irritator challengeri, was named after Professor Challenger, a character in Arthur Conan Doyle's novels, specifically The Lost World.

facts.statement: A detailed redescription of the specimen was published in 2002 after technician Diane M. Scott extracted the skull bones under the supervision of Hans-Dieter Sues.
facts.quote: Under the supervision of American paleontologist Hans-Dieter Sues, technician Diane M. Scott from the University of Toronto Mississauga assumed the task of fully extracting the skull bones from the rock, allowing for a detailed redescription in 2002.

facts.statement: Irritator shares dental features with Spinosaurus, including straight conical tooth crowns, thin enamel, unserrated edges, and lengthwise fluting.
facts.quote: Sues and colleagues regarded the African and possibly South American genus Spinosaurus as the most similar taxon to Irritator, because they shared many dental features, including mostly straight conical tooth crowns, thin enamel, well-defined edges with no serrations, and lengthwise fluting.

facts.statement: The specimen most probably originates from the Romualdo Formation.
facts.quote: the specimen most probably stems from the Romualdo Formation (previously designated the Romualdo Member of the then Santana Formation).

facts.statement: Local dealers suggested the fossil came from near the village of Buxexé at a height of approximately 650 meters.
facts.quote: Questioning of local fossil dealers hinted at a locality near the village of Buxexé close to Santana Do Cariri at the flank of the Chapada do Araripe, at a height of approximately 650 m.

facts.statement: Irritator challengeri was the first dinosaur described from the Romualdo Formation and holds the record for the most completely preserved spinosaurid skull.
facts.quote: Irritator challengeri was the first dinosaur described from the Romualdo Formation, and its holotype specimen represents the most completely preserved spinosaurid skull known.

facts.statement: Angaturama limai, a spinosaurid from the same time and place, was described by Alexander W. A. Kellner and Diogenes de Almeida Campos in February 1996.
facts.quote: Angaturama limai, another spinosaurid from the same time and place as Irritator challengeri, was described by the Brazilian paleontologists Alexander W. A. Kellner and Diogenes de Almeida Campos in February 1996.

facts.statement: Multiple authors from 2002 to 2015 supported the conclusion that Angaturama is a junior synonym of Irritator.
facts.quote: Authors including Éric Buffetaut and Mohamed Ouaja in 2002, Cristiano Dal Sasso and colleagues in 2005, Tor G. Bertin in 2010, Darren Naish in 2013, and Madani Benyoucef and colleagues in 2015 supported this conclusion.

facts.statement: Kellner and Campos argued in 2000 and 2005 that the fossils belong to two different genera, citing differences in lateral flattening.
facts.quote: Kellner and Campos in 2000 and Brazilian paleontologist Elaine B. Machado and Kellner in 2005 expressed the opinion that the fossils come from two different genera, and that the holotype of Angaturama limai was clearly more laterally flattened than that of Irritator challengeri.

facts.statement: In 2023, Schade and colleagues could not confirm tooth position overlap due to differing interpretations, leaving the issue unresolved.
facts.quote: In 2023, German paleontologist Marco Schade and colleagues could not confirm the overlap in tooth positions due to interpreting them differently, and could not provide information to resolve the issue.

facts.statement: In 2004, Brazilian paleontologists Jonathas Bittencourt and Kellner assigned a spinal column fragment (MN 4743-V) from the Romualdo Formation to the Spinosauridae family.
facts.quote: In 2004, parts of a spinal column (MN 4743-V) were unearthed at the formation.

facts.statement: The most complete spinosaurid specimen found in the Romualdo Formation is MN 4819-V, a partial skeleton that lacks a skull.
facts.quote: The most complete spinosaur specimen retrieved from the Romualdo Formation is MN 4819-V, a partial skeleton lacking the skull.

facts.statement: In 2018, Tito Aureliano and colleagues described LPP-PV-0042, a left tibia fragment from a particularly large spinosaurid individual.
facts.quote: In 2018, Tito Aureliano and his team described LPP-PV-0042, part of a left tibia from a particularly large individual.

facts.statement: Most spinosaurid fossils from the Romualdo Formation were collected under uncontrolled circumstances for the illegal fossil trade.
facts.quote: As is common with fossils from the Araripe Basin, the majority of spinosaurid material from the Romualdo Formation was collected under uncontrolled circumstances for use in the illegal fossil trade.

facts.statement: A replica skeleton of Angaturama, based on Romualdo Formation postcranial material, became the first large carnivorous Brazilian dinosaur displayed to the public in March 2009.
facts.quote: It was the centerpiece of the Dinossauros no Sertão (Dinosaurs of Sertão) exhibit, which opened to the public in March 2009, becoming the first large carnivorous Brazilian dinosaur to be put on display.

facts.statement: A fire at the National Museum of Rio de Janeiro in September 2018 likely destroyed the exhibited Angaturama skeleton and associated fossil elements.
facts.quote: In September 2018, a fire broke out at the palace housing the Museu Nacional, largely destroying the fossil collections and possibly the exhibited Angaturama skeleton and fossil elements.

facts.statement: Even at its maximum estimated size, Irritator was smaller than other known spinosaurids.
facts.quote: Even by maximal size estimates, Irritator was smaller than other known spinosaurids.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Irritator's length at 7.5 meters and weight at 1 ton.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul calculated its length at 7.5 m and weight at 1 t.

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimated Irritator's length at 8 meters and weight between 0.9 and 3.6 tons.
facts.quote: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. published a higher estimate of 8 m, with a weight between 0.9 to 3.6 t.

facts.statement: Dougal Dixon estimated Irritator to be 6 meters long and 2 meters high.
facts.quote: Estimates by Dougal Dixon were lower at 6 m long and 2 m high.

facts.statement: Scaling studies by Aureliano and colleagues estimated the Irritator holotype at 6.5 meters long and the Angaturama holotype at 8.3 meters long.
facts.quote: When scaled by Aureliano and colleagues, the reconstructions from the study by Sales and Schultz provided a length of 6.5 m for the Irritator challengeri holotype, and 8.3 m for the Angaturama limai holotype.

facts.statement: Unfused skull bones in the Irritator holotype indicate that the specimen belonged to a subadult individual.
facts.quote: Some of the skull bones of the former holotype had not yet fully co-ossified (fused), indicating that the specimen belonged to a subadult.

facts.statement: Spinosaurids from the Romualdo Formation may have reached sizes greater than those estimated for Irritator.
facts.quote: However, spinosaurids from the Romualdo Formation possibly attained greater sizes.

facts.statement: Based on a tibia fragment, Aureliano and colleagues estimated the length of the individual represented by LPP-PV-0042 at roughly 10 meters.
facts.quote: Although LPP-PV-0042 is represented only by a tibia fragment, Aureliano and colleagues estimated its length at roughly 10 m.

facts.statement: Unlike Baryonyx, Irritator's lacrimal bone did not form a bony horn core.
facts.quote: Unlike in Baryonyx, Irritators lacrimal did not form a bony horn core.

facts.statement: Irritator possessed a thin sagittal crest made of elongate nasal bones that extended along the skull midline to just above the eye.
facts.quote: A thin sagittal crest, constructed from the elongate nasal bones, extended along the skull midline before stopping just above the eye in a slightly flattened bulge.

facts.statement: While the full shape of Irritator's crest is unknown, similar spinosaurid crests likely served a display function.
facts.quote: Although the complete shape and height of this structure is unknown in Irritator, these head crests were commonplace in spinosaurids, having possibly served a display function when the animal was alive.

facts.statement: Irritator had straight or faintly recurved conical teeth with sharply defined but unserrated edges.
facts.quote: Irritator had straight or only faintly recurved conical teeth, bearing sharply defined but unserrated edges.

facts.statement: Irritator's teeth featured flutes, or lengthwise ridges, a common trait among spinosaurids.
facts.quote: Flutes (lengthwise ridges) were present on its tooth crowns, a common dental trait among spinosaurids.

facts.statement: Irritator's teeth were circular in cross-section, unlike the laterally flattened teeth of most theropods.
facts.quote: Irritators teeth were circular in cross section, as opposed to the laterally flattened condition of most theropod teeth.

facts.statement: Nine teeth are preserved in each maxilla of the Irritator holotype, with traces of a tenth tooth found in the rock matrix.
facts.quote: Both of Irritators maxillae preserve nine teeth, although the left maxilla's tooth crowns are more intact, and there are traces of a tenth tooth in the rock matrix.

facts.statement: CT scans revealed that Irritator had replacement teeth on both sides of its upper jaw.
facts.quote: CT scans performed on the specimen revealed replacement teeth on both sides of the upper jaw.

facts.statement: The front of Angaturama's snout was expanded into a spoon-shaped terminal rosette, a characteristic feature of spinosaurids.
facts.quote: The front of the snout was expanded, forming the spoon-shaped terminal rosette characteristic of spinosaurids.

facts.statement: A small bulge on the frontmost upper border of Angaturama's premaxilla overhung the base of its crest.
facts.quote: The frontmost upper border of the premaxilla had a small bulge that overhung the base of the crest.

facts.statement: Angaturama possessed strongly extended, straight, unserrated conical teeth measuring 6 to 40 mm in length that were singly embedded.
facts.quote: The strongly extended and straight teeth with unserrated conical crowns, which measured 6 to 40 mm in length, were singly embedded.

facts.statement: Irritator had a comparatively large, oval, sideways-facing opening called the mandibular fenestra in its lower jaw.
facts.quote: The mandibular fenestra, a sideways-facing opening in the lower jaw, was oval and comparatively large.

facts.statement: The partial skeleton MN 4819-V includes a largely intact pelvis, some back and tail vertebrae, five hip vertebrae, parts of the right shin, calf, thigh, and forearm bones.
facts.quote: MN 4819-V comprises a largely intact pelvis, some dorsal (back) and caudal (tail) vertebrae, five sacral (hip) vertebrae, a partial right tibia and fibula (shin and calf bones), most of the right femur (thigh bone), and part of an ulna (forearm bone).

facts.statement: Like all spinosaurids, the claw on the first finger, or thumb, of Irritator was enlarged.
facts.quote: Like in all spinosaurids, the claw of the first finger (the "thumb") was enlarged.

facts.statement: Elongated neural spines on the sacrum would have been covered in skin to form a sail down the animal's back.
facts.quote: In life, these would have been covered in skin, forming a "sail" down the animal's back.

facts.statement: Kellner resolved Irritator as a spinosaurid and synonymized the family Irritatoridae with Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: Kellner resolved Irritator as a spinosaurid and synonymized Irritatoridae with that family.

facts.statement: Oliver W. M. Rauhut assigned Irritator to the family Baryonychidae in 2003.
facts.quote: Irritator was then assigned to the Baryonychidae along with Angaturama, Baryonyx, Suchomimus, and Spinosaurus by Oliver W. M. Rauhut in 2003.

facts.statement: Holtz and colleagues considered the family Baryonychidae synonymous with Spinosauridae in 2004.
facts.quote: Holtz and colleagues in 2004 considered the Baryonychidae synonymous with Spinosauridae, and moved these genera to the latter family.

facts.statement: Irritator is placed within the superfamily Megalosauroidea, with Spinosauridae possibly being a sister taxon to Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: As spinosaurids, Irritator and Angaturama are placed within the superfamily Megalosauroidea, with Spinosauridae being a possible sister taxon to the Megalosauridae.

facts.statement: Sereno and colleagues placed Irritator in the subfamily Spinosaurinae and Baryonyx, Suchomimus, and Cristatusaurus in Baryonychinae.
facts.quote: Sereno and colleagues defined two subfamilies within the Spinosauridae based on craniodental (skull and tooth) characteristics. They were Spinosaurinae, where they placed Spinosaurus and Irritator; and Baryonychinae, to which they assigned Baryonyx, Suchomimus, and Cristatusaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers theorized that Irritator likely had a partly fish-eating diet due to its elongated snout and unserrated conical teeth.
facts.quote: In 1996, Martill and colleagues theorized that Irritator challengeri, with its elongated snout and unserrated conical teeth, likely had at least a partly piscivorous (fish-eating) diet.

facts.statement: Smooth and homogeneous dental microwear in Irritator suggests it consumed soft food.
facts.quote: The dental microwear of Irritator was very smooth and homogenous, indicative of soft food consumption.

facts.statement: A 2007 study found that the stiff secondary palate and reduced antorbital fenestrae of Irritator made its skull more resistant to torsion during feeding.
facts.quote: In 2007, a finite-element analysis study by British paleontologist Emily J. Rayfield and colleagues found that these attributes, present in other spinosaurids as well, made the skull more resistant to torsion from prey item loads when feeding.

facts.statement: Irritator's nostrils were positioned far back to allow respiration while the jaw was underwater or holding prey.
facts.quote: The nostrils of Irritator were shifted far back from the snout tip; this, along with the secondary palate, which separated the animal's nasal passages from the inside of its mouth, made respiration possible even if most of the jaw was underwater or held prey.

facts.statement: The sagittal crest of Irritator indicates pronounced neck musculature needed to close jaws quickly against water resistance.
facts.quote: In particular, the sagittal crest of Irritator is an indication for pronounced neck musculature, which would have been necessary to close the jaws quickly against water resistance and withdraw the head rapidly.

facts.statement: A 3.3-meter wingspan pterosaur fossil was found with an Irritator tooth inserted in its neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: A tooth belonging to Irritator was discovered still inserted into the fossil neck vertebral column of an anhanguerid pterosaur, likely with a wingspan of 3.3 m.

facts.statement: A 2023 study suggests Irritator's lower jaws could rotate and open laterally like a pelican's to swallow large prey.
facts.quote: Examinations and digital reconstructions of Irritator published in 2023 by Schade et al., suggests that the lower jaws of this spinosaurid could rotate and open laterally, with a gape similar to that of modern pelicans; this would have allowed the theropod to swallow very large prey items.

facts.statement: Analysis revealed that Irritator had a very weak but rapid bite.
facts.quote: It was also discovered to have a very weak but rapid bite as a result of this analysis.

facts.statement: Studies reaffirm that Irritator likely possessed binocular vision and held its snout at an inclined orientation.
facts.quote: The study also reaffirms that Irritator likely possessed binocular vision and would have held its snout at an inclined orientation.

facts.statement: Irritator's broad lower jaw and narrowed frontals caused its eye sockets to face steeply inward, unlike the laterally facing orbits of most theropods.
facts.quote: In particular, the broad lower jaw and narrowed frontals of Irritator resulted in the orbits facing at a steep incline towards the midline of the skull, whereas most theropods had laterally facing orbits.

facts.statement: Irritator's skull traits allowed it to see above the waterline while submerged.
facts.quote: These traits would have permitted the animal to see above the waterline when submerged.

facts.statement: A 2018 CT scan of an Irritator tibia fragment revealed osteosclerosis, or high bone density.
facts.quote: In 2018, Aureliano and colleagues conducted an analysis on the Romualdo Formation tibia fragment. CT scanning of the specimen in the University of São Carlos revealed the presence of osteosclerosis (high bone density).

facts.statement: A 2018 publication argued that osteosclerosis would not have significantly changed a theropod's buoyancy.
facts.quote: The significance of these traits was questioned in a later 2018 publication, where Canadian paleobiologist Donald Henderson argued that osteosclerosis would not have changed a theropod's buoyancy to a significant extent.

facts.statement: Irritator possessed an enlarged flocculus, a brain structure associated with coordinating fast head movements.
facts.quote: The flocculus appears to be enlarged in taxa that rely on quick movements of the head body.

facts.statement: Analysis of the cochlear duct suggests Irritator could hear frequencies averaging 1,950 Hz with a bandwidth of 3,196 Hz.
facts.quote: They also noted that the relatively well-developed cochlear duct may have enable an average hearing frequency of 1,950 Hz with a frequency band width of 3,196 Hz.

facts.statement: Researchers estimated Irritator's overall hearing range was 350–3,550 Hz, placing its hearing ability between that of crocodiles and birds.
facts.quote: However, they considered these ranges as rough estimates and established an overall frequency range of 350–3,550 Hz, making Irritator to be placed under bird hearing but above crocodiles.

facts.statement: A 2026 study identified bone structures in Irritator's skull consistent with salt glands, similar to those found in seabirds and shorebirds.
facts.quote: In 2026, a paper by Andrea Cau and colleagues found osteological correlates in Irritator's skull that are consistent with the presence of salt glands, similar to those seen in many seabirds and shorebirds.

facts.statement: Irritator lived approximately 110 million years ago during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: Irritator and Angaturama are known from the Romualdo Formation, whose rocks are dated to the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous Period, about 110 million years ago.

facts.statement: Irritator inhabited a coastal lagoon environment with irregular freshwater influence and fluctuating sea levels.
facts.quote: The formation is interpreted as a coastal lagoon with irregular freshwater influence that contended with cycles of transgressing and regressing sea levels.

facts.statement: The climate where Irritator lived was tropical and similar to modern-day Brazil.
facts.quote: The climate of the formation was tropical and largely corresponded to today's Brazilian climate.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the scarcity of herbivorous dinosaurs in the area may indicate that local vegetation was too sparse to support large populations.
facts.quote: According to Naish and colleagues, the lack of herbivorous dinosaurs could mean that the local vegetation was scant and thus incapable of sustaining a large population of them.

facts.statement: Abundant carnivorous theropods in the region likely relied on aquatic life as their primary food source.
facts.quote: The abundant carnivorous theropods would have then likely turned to the lush aquatic life as a primary food source.

facts.statement: Paleontologists hypothesize that storms may have washed pterosaur and fish carcasses onto shorelines, providing carrion for theropods.
facts.quote: They also hypothesized that following storm events, pterosaur and fish carcasses might have washed up on the shoreline, providing theropods with plenty of carrion.

facts.statement: Researchers propose that niche partitioning occurred among animals in the lagoon, allowing them to feed on prey of different sizes and in different locations.
facts.quote: Aureliano and colleagues stated there must have, therefore, been some degree of niche partitioning, where different animals would have fed on prey of varied sizes and locations within the lagoon.

facts.statement: The Irritator holotype skull was discovered lying on its side.
facts.quote: The skull was found lying on its side.

facts.statement: Several bones from the back of the braincase and the lower jaw were lost before the Irritator holotype fossilized.
facts.quote: Preceding fossilization, several bones from the back of the braincase, as well as the dentary, splenial, coronoid, and right angular bones from the lower jaw, were lost.

facts.statement: Many bones from the rear of the skull became disarticulated and moved to different positions on the head before burial.
facts.quote: Other bones, mostly from the skull rear, had become disarticulated and displaced towards alternate regions of the head before burial.

facts.statement: In 2018, researchers argued that the Irritator holotype was buried in its natural habitat because its lower jaw remained attached to the skull, which would likely have detached if the carcass had floated at sea.
facts.quote: In 2018, Aureliano and colleagues argued against this scenario, stating that the Irritator challengeri holotype's mandible was preserved in articulation with the rest of the skull, whereas it would have likely detached had the carcass been floating at sea.

facts.statement: A 2026 joint declaration between Brazil and Germany announced the willingness of German authorities to return the Irritator holotype fossil to Brazil.
facts.quote: In April 2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil and the German Press Office shared the Joint Declaration signed during the 3rd German-Brazilian Intergovernmental Consultations, which stated that "both governments welcome the willingness of the State of Baden-Württemberg and the State Museum of Natural History in Stuttgart to hand over the Irritator challengeri fossil to Brazil".

facts.statement: Legal analysis concluded that the Brazilian state is the legal owner of the Irritator holotype and that the German museum likely did not acquire it in good faith.
facts.quote: A legal analysis of potential restitution of the holotype of Irritator challengeri concluded that the Brazilian state is the legal owner of the fossil and that the State Museum of Natural History most likely did not acquire good title to it in good faith.

facts.statement: A civil lawsuit to reclaim the fossil in Germany is barred by a 30-year statute of limitations.
facts.quote: A civil action of restitution under Article 985 of the German Civil Code is, however, precluded due to a statute of limitations of 30 years.

facts.statement: A 2025 Brazilian petition demanding the return of the Irritator fossil gathered over 34,600 signatures.
facts.quote: In April 2025, the Brazilian think tank Rede Patrimônio em Pauta (Heritage in Focus Network) published an online petition demanding the return of the Irritator to its region of origin and has gathered over 34,600 signatures.

facts.statement: The genus Irritator was named by Martill and colleagues in 1996.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Martill et al, 1996

facts.statement: The species Irritator challengeri was named by Martill and colleagues in 1996.
facts.quote: species_authority: Martill et al, 1996

facts.statement: Irritator is classified within the family Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Spinosauridae

facts.statement: Irritator lived approximately 110 million years ago during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 110 millones de años, en el Albiense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The fossil remains of Irritator were found in the Santana Formation in Brazil.
facts.quote: Encontrado en la Formación Santana, en Brasil

facts.statement: Irritator is known from a partial skull that lacks the anterior portion.
facts.quote: se conoce por solo un cráneo parcial al que le falta la porción anterior.

facts.statement: The species name challengeri honors Professor Challenger, a character from Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's novel The Lost World.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, I. challengeri, fue nombrada por el personaje de la novela de Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, El mundo perdido, el Profesor Challenger.

facts.statement: Many researchers consider the genus Irritator to be a synonym of Angaturama limai, which lived in the same location.
facts.quote: Este género es considerado por muchos como un sinónimo de Angaturama limai, que viviera en el mismo lugar y sitio que el Irritator.

facts.statement: Remains attributed to Angaturama appear to complete the Irritator skull, suggesting they may belong to the same specimen.
facts.quote: Los restos de este curiosamente parecen terminar el cráneo de Irritator, significando que podrían pertenecer al mismo espécimen.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the maximum length of Irritator at 7.5 meters and its weight at 1 tonne.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul calculó su longitud en 7,5 metros y su peso en 1 tonelada.

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimated a maximum length of 8 meters and a weight between 0.9 and 3.6 tonnes.
facts.quote: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. publicó una estimación más alta de 8 metros, con un peso entre 0,9 y 3,6 toneladas.

facts.statement: Dougal Dixon estimated a length of less than 6 meters and a height of 2 meters.
facts.quote: Dougal Dixon fueron menores a 6 metros de largo y 2 de alto.

facts.statement: Some skull bones of the holotype were not fully ossified, indicating the specimen was a subadult.
facts.quote: Algunos de los huesos del cráneo del holotipo aún no se habían osificado completamente, es decir fusionados, lo que indica que el espécimen pertenecía a un subadulto.

facts.statement: Brazilian paleontologists and legal experts disputed the study's claim that the fossil belonged to Germany and called for its return, with two of the study's authors signing the letter.
facts.quote: Brazilian paleontologists and legal specialists disputed this claim and called for the return of the fossil to Brazil, inter alia in an open letter to Petra Olschowski, State Minister of Science and Art of Baden-Württemberg; two authors of the criticised study were among the signatories.

facts.statement: Critics argue the Joint Declaration's wording missed the opportunity to acknowledge the fossil's illicit provenance and suppressed its decolonial implications.
facts.quote: This has been criticised as a missed opportunity to acknowledge the illicit provenance of the fossil, and as an attempt to distort the meaning of what, factually, is a return and suppress its legal, ethical, and decolonial implications along a North-South relationship of power.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Irritator is 16.5 cm tall and 10 cm wide, with an estimated total length of 60 cm.
facts.quote: El cráneo conservado tiene 16,5 centímetros De altura y 10 de ancho, su longitud total se ha estimado en aproximadamente 60 centímetros

facts.statement: Irritator had an elongated, low snout with relatively flat sides that angled slightly toward the midline of the skull.
facts.quote: Desde él se extendía un hocico alargado y bajo, con ambos lados relativamente planos y ligeramente en ángulo hacia la línea media del cráneo

facts.statement: A thin sagittal crest made of elongated nasal bones rose along the midline of the skull and stopped just above the eye as a slightly flattened bump.
facts.quote: Una cresta sagital delgada, construida a partir de los huesos nasales alargados, subía por la línea media del cráneo antes de detenerse justo encima del ojo en un bulto ligeramente aplanado

facts.statement: Like other spinosaurids, Irritator possessed a long bony structure in the palate called a secondary palate that separated the mouth from the nasal cavity.
facts.quote: Como otros en su familia , Irritador poseía una estructura larga y ósea en el paladar, llamada paladar secundario, que separa la boca de la cavidad nasal

facts.statement: The Irritator holotype is unique because it is one of the few non-avian dinosaur fossils found with a preserved stirrup bone.
facts.quote: El holotipo Irritator challengeri es único, ya que es uno de los poco fósiles de dinosaurios no aviares que se encuentran con un estribo conservado

facts.statement: The lower margin of the premaxillae was concave, reaching its deepest point at the sixth premaxillary tooth.
facts.quote: El margen inferior de los premaxilares era cóncavo, con la concavidad alcanzando su ápice en el sexto diente premaxilar

facts.statement: The front of the snout expanded to form a terminal rosette shaped like a spoon, a characteristic feature of spinosaurids.
facts.quote: La parte frontal del hocico se expandió, formando la roseta terminal en forma de cuchara característica de los espinosáuridos

facts.statement: Irritator had strongly extended, straight teeth with unflattened conical crowns measuring 6 to 40 mm in length that were embedded individually.
facts.quote: Los dientes fuertemente extendidos y rectos con coronas cónicas no rectificadas, que medían de 6 a 40 milímetros de longitud, se incrustaron individualmente

facts.statement: A 16 cm gap existed between the last premaxillary tooth and the first maxillary tooth.
facts.quote: Un diastema de 16 centímetros estuvo presente entre el último premaxilar y el primer diente maxilar

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Irritator challengeri is mostly complete but damaged in certain places, lacking only the snout tip and front of the jaw.
facts.quote: El cráneo holotipo de Irritator challengeri, aunque está muy dañado en ciertos lugares, está en gran parte completo, falta solo la punta del hocico y la parte delantera de la mandíbula

facts.statement: The nasal openings of Irritator were proportionally and absolutely smaller than in Suchomimus and Baryonyx, but larger than in Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: Las fosas nasales de Irritator fueron proporcionalmente y absolutamente más pequeñas que en Suchomimus y Baryonyx, pero más grandes que las de Spinosaurus

facts.statement: The sagittal crest of Angaturama was larger and extended further forward over the snout than in other known spinosaurids.
facts.quote: Esta cresta era más grande y se extendía más hacia adelante sobre el hocico que en otros espinosáuridos conocidos

facts.statement: The tooth arrangement indicates continuous tooth replacement where new teeth were pushed upward by old ones.
facts.quote: Esto indica reemplazo continuo de dientes donde los nuevos dientes fueron empujados hacia arriba por los viejos

facts.statement: Sales and Schultz proposed in 2017 that the maxillary tooth overlapped the premaxillary tooth in the holotype specimens.
facts.quote: según lo propuesto por Sales y Schultz en 2017

facts.statement: Researchers theorized in 1996 that Irritator challengeri likely had at least a partially piscivorous diet due to its elongated snout and unserrated conical teeth.
facts.quote: En 1996, Martill y sus colegas teorizaron que Irritator challengeri, con su hocico alargado y sus dientes cónicos no serrados, probablemente tenía al menos una dieta parcialmente piscívora.

facts.statement: The long conical teeth of Spinosaurids, which lacked serrated edges, were suitable for grasping and holding prey.
facts.quote: Los largos dientes cónicos, que en los espinosáuridos no poseían bordes serrados, eran adecuados para agarrar y sostener la presa.

facts.statement: A 2007 study by Emily J. Rayfield and colleagues found that Spinosaurid skulls were more resistant to torsion from prey loads when feeding.
facts.quote: En 2007, un estudio de análisis de elementos finitos realizado por la paleontóloga británica Emily J. Rayfield y sus colegas descubrió que estos atributos, presentes también en otros espinosáuridos, hicieron que el cráneo fuera más resistente a la torsión de las cargas de elementos de presa cuando se alimentaban.

facts.statement: The sagittal crest of Irritator indicates pronounced neck musculature necessary for closing jaws quickly against water resistance and withdrawing the head rapidly.
facts.quote: En particular, la cresta sagital de Irritator es una indicación de la musculatura del cuello pronunciada, que habría sido necesario para cerrar las mandíbulas rápidamente contra la resistencia al agua y retirar la cabeza rápidamente.

facts.statement: In 2015, Serjoscha W. Evers and colleagues found evidence of similar adaptations in the African spinosaurid Sigilmassasaurus.
facts.quote: En 2015, la paleontóloga alemana Serjoscha W. Evers y sus colegas encontraron evidencia de adaptaciones similares en el espinosáurido africano Sigilmassasaurus.

facts.statement: Sales and Schultz found in 2017 that Irritator and baryonychines may have relied more on smell for hunting than Spinosaurus due to larger, less retracted nostrils and more cranial space for nasal cavities.
facts.quote: Sales y Schultz en 2017 encontraron que Irritator y las barioniquinos podrían haber dependido más de su sentido del olfato para la caza que el Spinosaurus ya que tenían fosas nasales más grandes, menos retraídas y más espacio en sus cráneos para la cavidad nasal.

facts.statement: Spinosaurids shared with gharials an enlarged snout tip holding a series of interlocked rosette-shaped teeth useful for spearing and catching fish.
facts.quote: Otro rasgo de los espirosáuridos compartidos con los gaviales fue una punta de hocico agrandada que empuñaba una serie de dientes entrelazados en forma de roseta, útiles para empalar y atrapar peces.

facts.statement: In 2002, Sues and colleagues argued there was no reason to assume Spinosaurids specialized completely in fishing.
facts.quote: En 2002, Sues y sus colegas señalaron, sin embargo, que no habría razón para suponer que los Spinosauridae se especializaran completamente en la pesca.

facts.statement: In 2004, Naish and colleagues supported the theory that Irritator hunted aquatic and terrestrial animals as a coastal generalist and likely scavenged.
facts.quote: En 2004, Naish y sus colegas apoyaron la teoría de que Irritator cazaba animales acuáticos y terrestres como un generalista dentro del área costera y, además, probablemente buscaba carroña.

facts.statement: In 2018, Aureliano and colleagues presented a possible scenario for the food web of the Romualdo Formation.
facts.quote: En 2018, Aureliano y sus colegas presentaron un posible escenario para la red alimentaria de la Formación Romualdo.

facts.statement: Researchers proposed that spinosaurids in the formation may have hunted aquatic and terrestrial crocodiliforms, juveniles of their own species, turtles, and small to medium-sized dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Los investigadores propusieron que los espinoáuridos de la formación también pueden haber cazado crocodiliformes acuáticos y terrestres, juveniles de su propia especie, tortugas y dinosaurios de tamaño pequeño a mediano.

facts.quote: Parent group: Spinosaurinae
